Catalan

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [ˈkur.su]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic) [ˈkur.so]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈkuɾ.so]

Verb

[edit]

curso

  1. first-person singular present indicative of cursar

Galician

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Unknown.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈkuɾsʊ]

Noun

[edit]

curso m (plural cursos)

  1. (anatomy) rectum
    Synonym: recto

Etymology 2

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin cursus (“course, act of running”), from currō (“to run”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈkuɾsʊ]

Noun

[edit]

curso m (plural cursos)

  1. course (period of learning)
  2. course (path, route)

Latin

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈkʊr.soː]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈkur.so]

Etymology 1

[edit]
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ḱers-der.
Proto-Italic *korzō
Latin currō
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂yéti
Proto-Italic *-āō
Latin -ō
Latin -tō
Latin curso

    From currō (“run”) +‎ -tō.

    Verb

    [edit]

    cursō (present infinitive cursāre, perfect active cursāvī, supine cursātum); first conjugation, impersonal in the passive

    1. to run around; to run here and there

    Portuguese

    [edit]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
     
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈkuʁ.su/ [ˈkuh.su]
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈkuʁ.su/ [ˈkuh.su]
      • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /ˈkuɾ.su/
      • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ˈkuʁ.su/ [ˈkuχ.su]
      • (Caipira) IPA(key): /ˈkuɻ.su/
      • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈkuʁ.so/ [ˈkuh.so]
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈkuɾ.su/

    • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
    • Rhymes: (Brazil) -uʁsu, (Portugal) -uɾsu
    • Hyphenation: cur‧so

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    Borrowed from Latin cursus (“course, act of running”), from currō (“to run”). Compare the inherited doublet corso.

    Noun

    [edit]

    curso m (plural cursos)

    1. course (period of learning)
    2. course (path, route)
      Synonyms: percurso, caminho, rota
    3. watercourse
    Related terms
    [edit]
    • correr, cursar, cursista, cursivo, cursor, discurso, recurso

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

    Verb

    [edit]

    curso

    1. first-person singular present indicative of cursar

    Further reading

    [edit]

    • “curso”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

    Spanish

    [edit]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈkuɾso/ [ˈkuɾ.so]
    • Audio (Latin America pronounced sample):(file)
    • Rhymes: -uɾso
    • Syllabification: cur‧so

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    Borrowed from Latin cursus. See also coso, a doublet inherited from the same origin.

    Noun

    [edit]

    curso m (plural cursos)

    1. course, trajectory, route, direction
    2. class, course (learning program, as in a school)
      un curso intensivo ― a crash course
    3. course (path, sequence, development, or evolution)
    4. (colloquial, Mexico, Central America) diarrhea
      Synonym: diarrea
